findings.classification: definite source ordering defect; runtime manifestation not reproduced
findings.title: Cancelled/superseded preview tasks can overwrite the current frame
findings.producer_consumer: FeedPhotoMediaPreview, FeedVideoPreviewFrame, FeedPDFPreviewFrame and FeedMediaTeaserBlock supply URL/kind to one FeedAsyncMediaFrame @State image. .task(id: requestID) cancels an old request; detachedData/videoPreviewData translate cancellation to nil; the view unconditionally assigns that late nil.
findings.scenario: Same frame identity changes from uncached slow A to B. A is cancelled but its synchronous operationBody can finish later. B (including cache hit) publishes its image. A resumes with nil and line980 replaces B with fallback. Independently, the old @State image stays visible with B's caption/copyright until B completes because state has no request identity/reset.
findings.impact: Current photo/video/PDF/teaser preview can show unrelated previous content/metadata or be blanked by superseded work. Does not corrupt source files or persisted cards.
findings.target: Only the current live request may publish UI state; visible image must belong to current URL/kind.
findings.minimal_fix: Keep an immutable request snapshot; await into a local value and guard task cancellation before assigning. Reset or key the visible image by that snapshot so new metadata cannot accompany the previous request's image. No new ViewModel/protocol required. Also reject cancelled loader work before MainActor reconstruction/cache insertion where appropriate.
findings.verification: After separate authorization: deterministic A-slow -> B-fast/cache-hit -> A-cancelled completion (including nil) plus disappear/reappear; verify B persists and no old image with new metadata. Exercise all current callers and fallback/caption/copyright. Build both affected hosts under actual Swift6 complete-concurrency settings; iPhone Simulator18.2+27 only.
findings.disposition: Parent adjudicates; fix before expansion/merge of affected path, no source edit here.

findings.confidence: high for missing source bound; medium for operational impact
findings.title: Video frames enter PNG/UI cache without the photo/PDF pixel bounds
findings.producer_consumer: FeedVideoPreviewFrame requests .video for a 220pt preview. AVAssetImageGenerator has transform but no maximumSize; result.image is encoded directly, then reconstructed on MainActor and cached. Photo is capped at1200 max pixels and PDF at640x420; cache supplies countLimit160 only, no object costs/byte budget.
findings.scenario: A valid high-resolution video reaches the existing preview caller; extracted frame is forwarded without any code-imposed pixel cap. Several such previews can be retained under the160-item cache policy.
findings.impact: PNG work, returned bytes, UI image reconstruction and retained image memory follow the extracted video frame size rather than a preview envelope. Static review establishes the missing limit, not actual OOM/jank or a measured footprint.
findings.target: Declare/enforce video thumbnail dimensions before extraction/encoding and account cache retention by decoded cost, with product-appropriate eviction/pressure policy.
findings.minimal_fix: Set generator.maximumSize to the justified existing preview pixel policy before image(at:); keep preferred-track transform. Cost cache items from decoded dimensions/bytesPerRow and set a reviewed byte budget if cache memory must be claimed bounded. Preserve source video, thumbnail semantics, kind+URL identity, captions/teaser behavior.
findings.verification: After matching grant: high-resolution/rotated-video boundary verifies returned thumbnail dimensions/cost; cancel/malformed/missing video still fallback. Both host builds; iPhone Simulator18.2+27 UI for image/fallback/metadata. Profiling only if delegated for a concrete remaining performance claim; no physical/iPad checks.
findings.disposition: Parent adjudicates; bound producer before expanding this media path. Resource thresholds require explicit app policy, no invented universal budget.

hypotheses.statement: PDF thumbnail preparation reads the entire file into Data before PDFDocument(data:), with no local byte cap. Output pixels are bounded but input bytes/parse work are not bounded here.
hypotheses.missing_evidence: Upstream PDF file-size/page/complexity admission contract and accepted maximum files. Media model contains only a URL, no enforceable size contract; source producers are outside scope.
hypotheses.proposal: Parent first trace the actual PDF import/publish producer and maximum accepted sizes. Then choose URL-backed/lazy document loading or an enforced byte envelope if needed; retaining FileHandle readToEnd cannot itself support bounded-input memory claim. No huge fixture created here.

hypotheses.statement: Cache misses have no in-flight coalescing or aggregate admission bound. Cancellation is forwarded correctly to detached task handles, but synchronous file/decode/draw/PNG segments run to their next cancellation check. For video, task cancellation forwarding is visible; AVAssetImageGenerator cancellation latency without cancelAllCGImageGeneration is not established.
hypotheses.missing_evidence: Actual concurrent caller count/repeated-scroll workload, duplicate same-key miss exposure, framework cancellation behavior, measured task growth/latency. No leak/unbounded-growth or generator API failure asserted.
hypotheses.proposal: If user-visible resource failure remains after request gating/video sizing, observe a finite repeated-scroll/cancel workload under matching grant; add coalescing/admission only for demonstrated need.

hypotheses.statement: Request/cache identity uses kind+raw URL only. Replacing file contents at the same URL, or recreating a fallback filename with different content, would keep an existing cached thumbnail/task identity.
hypotheses.missing_evidence: Are published composer media filenames immutable and unique? Exact storage/publish producer contract is outside the authorized scope.
hypotheses.proposal: Parent inspect AppFileStorageDomains.composerMediaPath(existingFilename:)/composerMediaFileURL(for:) and the actual publisher only if same-path replacement is a supported path. Do not add mtime/stat in body or rewrite persisted references speculatively.

false_positives_rejected: SwiftUI .task cancellation alone does not suppress subsequent @State assignment; cannot call F1 fixed by existing cancellation handlers.
Task.detached is not automatically a leak: both wrappers store handle, await value and forward cancellation.
MainActor cache/UIImage ownership is legitimate; no actor race or blanket MainActor violation inferred from the annotation alone.
No synchronous thumbnail generation/file access in the reviewed body path. Resolver is in async renderer path; its executor/effective toolchain is not inferred beyond declared settings.
First-photo-only rendering, audio placeholder, optional teaser+media stack and nil fallback are existing semantics, not invented defects.
Cache is not wholly unbounded: it has countLimit160. Actual resident bytes, NSCache eviction guarantees, memory-pressure response and >250ms UI hang were not measured.
Failure/loading sharing a fallback is existing optional-preview behavior; no invented spinner/retry/error UI requirement.
Source models are Codable/Sendable narrow metadata with explicit photos-or-file enum; no schema change proposed.
strengths: No media processing in inspected SwiftUI body.
Detached image/PDF heavy work and video worker; Data crosses boundary and UI objects remain MainActor-owned.
Cancellation forwarded, checks before/after sync bodies; FileHandle closes via defer.
Image downsample transform/max1200 and bounded first-page PDF context.
Placeholder dimensions/caption/copyright preserved; missing/empty files return nil; png failure returns nil without fake success.
Cache keyed by media kind prevents cross-kind collision.
